lines.text: In an online strategy game, the server sees the whole map. On a public blockchain, everyone does.
So you either trust whoever runs the game, or you keep no secrets.
Veil is a third way: a war in the clouds where nobody can see the map. Not the players. Not even me.
The game is the demonstration. Anything that needs a secret on a public chain works the same way: cards, auctions, sealed bids.
I open the link. No wallet, no sign-up. A relayer creates my NEAR account and pays every fee.
I open a lobby and send a friend one link. When every seat is taken, the war starts by itself.
I see my capital and nothing else. The real map lives where nobody can look.
Inside an OutLayer enclave: Intel T D X hardware running the game engine in memory even its operator can't read.
I march, recruit, and seal my orders. My browser encrypts them to a key that exists only inside that enclave.
The NEAR contract holds the ciphertext and keeps the clock. Everyone sees that I sealed, never what.
Once everyone has sealed, the enclave opens the orders, fights the battles, and sends each player only their own view.
The dice come from a verifiable random function. The contract checks every roll's proof before it accepts the turn.
Empty seats go to AI warlords. They decide inside the enclave too, from their own fog only.
Each has its own wallet and trades what it knows. I buy intel on an island under my cloud.
Or a truce, so it holds back. Prices change every turn, and every trade is part of the rules.
When the war ends, the enclave publishes everything it hid: every order, every roll, and the match key.
My browser re-runs the whole match with the same Rust code and checks it against the chain.
Verified.
Hidden while you play. Provable when it ends. That's what Veil is here to show.
Winnings get the same care. Through Chain Signatures, my NEAR account controls an address on Base: no second wallet.
On mainnet, NEAR Intents carries the winnings across. Here on testnet, a faucet stands in.
I seal them into Gloam's private pool. Later, a zero-knowledge proof cashes them out to any address I choose.
Gloam's relay sends that transaction, so my address never appears next to it.
Mouse, touch, keyboard or gamepad: one radial menu gives every order.
Veil. A strategy game where even the developer can't see the map. Play it at veil dot mister fomo labs dot x y z.
